title: Minimum Knight Moves
prompt: On an infinite chessboard, a knight starts at square `(0, 0)`. Given a target square `(x, y)`, return the minimum number of knight moves needed to reach it. A knight has 8 possible moves, each moving two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular.

examples.explanation: A single knight move from (0,0) lands directly on (2,1).
Four knight moves are needed to travel from (0,0) to (5,5).

hints: Since every knight move costs the same, BFS from the start finds the minimum number of moves to any square.

The board is infinite, but by symmetry you only ever need to search within the bounding box around (0,0) and the target, expanded by a small margin — or simply bound coordinates to something like [-2, |x|+2] x [-2, |y|+2] to keep the search finite.
Use a visited set to avoid revisiting squares (BFS can otherwise re-explore the same square many times), and stop as soon as the target is dequeued.

solution.approach: Because every move has equal cost, the fewest moves to reach the target is exactly a shortest-path problem, solvable with BFS from (0,0). Although the board is infinite, the search only needs to explore a bounded region around the origin and target (clamping coordinates to a small margin beyond the target's bounding box) since wandering further away can never produce a shorter path. A visited set prevents revisiting the same square, keeping the BFS efficient.
